title: WAL commit-path bundle: widen group-commit window and writer flush batch
configuration_cause: commit_delay=100us with commit_siblings=2 opens a fixed per-commit sleep that rarely collects siblings at 5 terminals, while wal_writer_flush_after=0 disables writer-side flush batching; WAL sync average 0.111ms and wal_waiting_backends p95=1 persist.
mechanism: The incumbent pays a fixed 100us commit_delay on every commit but commit_siblings=2 means the window activates almost always, adding latency without reliably coalescing fsyncs; wal_writer_flush_after=0 forces the WAL writer to flush per write. Widening commit_delay to 200us with commit_siblings=3 makes the window activate only when >=3 backends are committing, so the sleep is amortized over a real group, and setting wal_writer_flush_after=64 (512kB) lets the writer batch background WAL writes. Together these reduce per-commit fsync frequency and WAL queueing, freeing terminal capacity for GetUserTweets.
query_effect: GetUserTweets is read-dominated and unaffected directly; reduced commit-path queueing lowers InsertTweet latency and frees terminal capacity shared with GetUserTweets.
expected_tps_effect: Small increase (>=0.3%) if WAL sync coalescing reduces commit stalls; neutral if WAL is not the binding constraint.
expected_latency_effect: InsertTweet p95 decreases; GetUserTweets p50/p95 unchanged.

predictions.rationale: Larger writer flush batch and a group-commit window that only activates with >=3 siblings coalesce fsyncs, lowering average sync time.
Fewer per-commit fsyncs reduce backends waiting on WAL.
Reduced commit-path queueing frees terminal capacity, raising completed transaction TPS.

alternatives.statement: WAL sync is already fast (0.111ms) and not the binding constraint; the bundle yields no measurable TPS change and sync_average_ms stays within noise.
Widening commit_delay to 200us adds latency without collecting siblings, so InsertTweet p95 rises and TPS falls.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent commit_delay=100/commit_siblings=2 activates the sleep on nearly every commit without reliably grouping, and wal_writer_flush_after=0 disables writer batching. Raising commit_siblings to 3 gates the window to real groups and enabling a 512kB writer flush batch coalesces background WAL writes, targeting the persistent wal_wait anomaly.

nodes.label: Group-commit window gated to real sibling groups plus writer-side flush batching coalesce fsyncs

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Widen from 100us to 200us within safe [0,1000]; paired with commit_siblings=3 the window activates only for real groups, amortizing the sleep.
Raise from 2 to 3 within safe [0,20]; with 5 terminals, 3 siblings gates the window to genuine concurrent commits instead of nearly every commit.
Set from 0 to 64 (8kB units = 512kB) within safe [0,1024]; enables writer-side flush batching so background WAL writes coalesce instead of flushing per write.
